name: Timor-Leste
summary_text: Timor-Leste is workable for trans visitors. Same-sex conduct is legal, the constitution's equality provisions have been read inclusively, and Dili hosts an annual Pride march with government participation — remarkable for a young, Catholic-majority nation. There is no legal gender recognition and services are thin, but there is no documented pattern of police targeting or anti-trans violence, and the small community (CODIVA, Arco Iris) operates openly.

sources.title: Pride Guide - Timor-Leste | The Australian Volunteers Program
sources.claim_summary: Australian Volunteers Program Pride Guide for Timor-Leste: country snapshot of the local LGBTQIA+ context - same-sex acts decriminalised in 1975; the 2011 UN HRC joint statement on SOGI adopted; practical guidance for volunteers on local law, protections and living openly.

sources.title: Laws and Policies Analytics | Joint Analysis | Timor-Leste
sources.claim_summary: UNAIDS Laws and Policies Analytics for Timor-Leste filtered to transgender-related laws and policies - database interface showing the legal framework affecting trans people.

sources.title: Over 80 Nations Support Statement at Human Rights Council on LGBT Rights - U.S. Mission to International Organizations in Geneva
sources.claim_summary: US Mission in Geneva (March 2011): post on LGBT rights in the UN context - US diplomatic advocacy for SOGI rights at the Human Rights Council, relevant to Timor-Leste's international human-rights environment.

sources.title: Behind Timor-Leste's Pride – New Naratif
sources.claim_summary: New Naratif (June 2018) by Sophie Raynor: 'Behind Timor-Leste's Pride' - the first-ever Pride parade (2017) garnered international attention and a televised PM endorsement, but 'the shine of a single event belies a grittier day-to-day'; organiser Natalino Guterres received 'Gay people are monsters' messages from his own brother - rejection and reconciliation within families.

sources.title: Asia's Youngest Nation Celebrates 2nd LGBT Parade
sources.claim_summary: VOA (July 2018): Asia's youngest nation held its second LGBT pride parade - Timor-Leste cemented its role as a regional LGBT rights leader while neighbours Indonesia and Malaysia turn hostile; PM Rui Maria de Araujo: 'discrimination, disrespect and abuse toward people, because of their sexual orientation or gender identity, does not provide any benefit to our nation.'

sources.title: East Timor celebrates third LGBTQI Pride Parade - Star Observer
sources.claim_summary: Star Observer (July 2019): East Timor celebrated its third LGBTQI Pride - ~3,000 people joined the 'Marsa Diversidade' in Dili, six times the 2017 turnout; President Francisco Guterres: 'I am a President for all people!... I ask everyone to see diversity as our nation's wealth'; homosexuality legal since 1975.
